title: Personal Credit Cards: Courtesy Reversal Allowances by Tier
content:
Personal Credit Cards allow a limited number of goodwill reversals each rolling 365 days: courtesy reversals of late payment fees, which also require an unbroken record of on-time payments immediately before the late statement, and courtesy reversals of residual (trailing) interest. The allowances are counted per customer across all of that customer's cards.

| Tier | Courtesy late fee reversals per rolling 365 days | On-time payments needed immediately before the late statement | Courtesy trailing interest reversals per rolling 365 days |
|---|---|---|---|
| Secured Visa | 1 | 6 | 1 |
| College Rewards Visa | 1 | 3 | 1 |
| Platinum Low Rate Visa | 1 | 6 | 1 |
| Cash Rewards Visa | 1 | 6 | 1 |
| Travel Rewards Visa Signature | 2 | 3 | 1 |
| Visa Infinite Private Client | 3 | 0 | 2 |

## Reading the table

- An allowance figure is a ceiling that the customer's count of earlier courtesy reversals must stay below. With an allowance of 1, a courtesy reversal is possible only when no courtesy reversal of that kind was granted in the rolling period.
- A requirement of 0 on-time payments, as on Visa Infinite Private Client, means the payment-history test is always met.

> Hypothetical illustration: a Travel Rewards Visa Signature cardholder already received one courtesy late fee reversal eight months ago. The count of 1 is below the allowance of 2, so the allowance is not exhausted; a second courtesy reversal in the same rolling period would bring the count to 2, and a third would then be out of reach.
